summary.text: Al Stirpe is the incumbent Democratic and Working Families Party candidate for New York State Assembly District 127 in the November 3, 2026 general election.

A former software and technology company executive, he first served in the Assembly from 2006 to 2010, was elected again in 2012, and chairs the Committee on Economic Development, Job Creation, Commerce and Industry.

paragraphs.text: Stirpe was raised in Clyde, where his family owned and operated Albert's Restaurant for more than 25 years, and he earned a bachelor's degree in economics from the University of Notre Dame.

He worked as a financial analyst for General Electric in Syracuse and became chief financial officer of CID Technologies, formed from the spin-off of GE's Electronic Camera Operation; after its 1994 sale to Thermo Electron he founded Qube Software, Inc., where he was president.
Stirpe was first elected to the Assembly in 2006 and served until 2010.
In 2011 and 2012 he was executive director of Synapse Sustainability Trust, an environmental not-for-profit, and he was elected to the Assembly again in 2012, serving the 127th District since then.
He is also a member of the Agriculture, Alcoholism and Drug Abuse, and Higher Education committees.
His official biography says he lives in Cicero with his wife, Chele, and has run a blood drive with the Red Cross for 19 years.
